title: Task-Aware Digital Twin State Updates in Resource-Constrained Edge IoT
content: Digital twins deployed in edge IoT environments require timely state updates while operating under limited communication and computational resources. This study proposes a task-aware method for managing digital twin state updates by jointly selecting the state component, update detail level, and processing location under explicit resource budgets. The method uses a one-step heuristic that ranks feasible update candidates according to expected quality gain, task-dependent importance, staleness, and normalized network and computation cost. It was evaluated on a physical ESP32-based IoT testbed using a common 180-cycle reference trace, with 179 cycles used for comparison across six adaptive scenarios and six baseline scenarios. Under the normal budget, the proposed method reduced average network and computation costs by 5.26% and 11.02%, respectively, compared with periodic and freshness-based baselines. Under the limited event-monitoring profile, the reductions were 3.97% and 10.38%, while maintaining a maximum temperature and humidity staleness of one cycle. Under the critical event-monitoring budget, prolonged starvation of temperature and humidity was observed, revealing a limitation of the current heuristic. The results show that the method provides task-dependent resource reallocation rather than universal improvement across all metrics.
